items.zh: 勝處等至遍處等至。如前已說。復次，云何無想三摩鉢底？謂已離遍淨欲，未離上欲，求出離想作意為先，諸心心法滅。問：以何方便入此等至？答：觀想如病、如癰、如箭，入第四靜慮，修背想作意，於所生起種種想中厭背而住。唯謂無想寂靜微妙，於無想中持心而住。如是漸次離諸所緣，心便寂滅。於此生中，亦入亦起。若生於彼，唯入不起。其想若生，便從彼沒。
items.en: The mastery-attainments and the totality-attainments are as already explained. Furthermore, what is the no-perception attainment? For one who has left the desire of the Universally-Pure [third dhyāna] but not the higher desire, taking as its precondition the attention of permanent escape from perception, the minds and mental factors cease. Question: by what means does one enter this attainment? Answer: contemplating perception as a disease, a boil, an arrow, one enters the fourth dhyāna and cultivates the attention of turning back from perception, wearying of and turning away from the various perceptions that arise, dwelling [in the thought] "only the perception-less is quiescent and subtle," holding the mind in the perception-less. Thus, gradually leaving all objects, the mind becomes quiescent. In this present life one both enters and emerges from it; but if reborn there, one only enters and does not emerge — and when perception arises, one falls from there.

items.title: The Cessation Attainment: Entering It, and the Order in Which the Formations Still

items.zh: 復次，云何滅盡三摩鉢底？謂已離無所有處欲，暫安住想作意為先，諸心心法滅。問：以何方便入此等至？答：若諸聖者，已離無所有處欲。或依非想非非想處相而入於定，或依滅盡相而入於定。依非想非非想處相而入定者，謂於此上心深生厭捨，非想非非想處進趣所緣皆滅盡故，心便寂滅。依滅盡相而入定者，亦復如是。
items.en: Furthermore, what is the cessation attainment? For one who has left the desire of the sphere of nothingness, taking as its precondition the attention that wishes to abide at rest for a while, the minds and mental factors cease. Question: by what means does one enter this attainment? Answer: a noble one who has left the desire of the sphere of nothingness enters the concentration either by way of the mark of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, or by way of the mark of cessation. To enter by the mark of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is to generate a deep weariness and relinquishment towards these two minds, so that, all the objects that sphere advances towards being extinguished, the mind falls quiescent. To enter by the mark of cessation is likewise.

items.zh: 將欲趣入滅盡定時，有二種法多有所作。謂奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。云何奢摩他？云何毘鉢舍那？云何此二多有所作？謂於此義中，八次第定名奢摩他，所有聖慧名毘鉢舍那。於此二中隨闕一種，即不能入滅盡等至；要具此二，方能趣入。是故此二多有所作。問：入滅定時，云何次第滅三種行？答：此有二種。謂行時、住時。若於行時，亦起言說。於初靜慮有此作用，有語行故。若於住時，從第二靜慮已上次第定力，彼三種行次第而滅。當知出時，由逆次第次第而起。
items.en: When about to enter the cessation attainment, two things have much to do with it: calm and insight. Here the eight successive attainments are the calm, and all the noble wisdom is the insight; lacking either of the two, one cannot enter the cessation attainment — one must possess both to enter, so these two have much to do with it. Question: on entering the cessation attainment, in what order do the three formations cease? Answer: this is of two kinds, the moving-time and the abiding-time. In the moving-time one still gives rise to speech — the first dhyāna has this function, since it has the speech-formation. In the abiding-time, by the force of the successive attainments from the second dhyāna upwards, those three formations cease in order. Know that on emerging, they arise in order, in reverse.

items.title: Two Puzzles of Cessation, and the Three Contacts on Emerging

items.zh: 問：滅盡定中，諸心心法並皆滅盡。云何說識不離於身？答：由不變壞諸色根中，有能執持轉識種子阿賴耶識不滅盡故，後時彼法從此得生。問：入滅定時，無有分別：我當入定，我當出定。正在定時，心寂滅故，遠離加行。將出定時，心先滅故，亦無作意。云何能入？云何能出？答：先於其心善修治故。若有諸行、諸狀、諸相，能入於定、能出於定，於彼修習、極多修習；由修習故，任運能入、任運能出。
items.en: Question: in the cessation attainment, all minds and mental factors are wholly extinguished — how then is it said that consciousness is not separate from the body? Answer: because within the unspoiled material faculties there is the storehouse-consciousness, which holds the seeds of the active consciousnesses and is not extinguished; so that afterwards those [active] dharmas arise again from it. Question: on entering the cessation attainment there is no thought "I shall enter, I shall exit"; while in it, the mind being quiescent, one is far from any application; and about to emerge, the mind having already ceased, there is no attention either. How can one enter, and how can one exit? Answer: because one has beforehand well cultivated the mind. If there are the practices, states, and marks by which one can enter and emerge, and one cultivates them, cultivates them exceedingly much — then by that cultivation one enters spontaneously and emerges spontaneously.

items.zh: 云何出滅定時觸三種觸？一、不動觸，二、無所有觸，三、無相觸。謂出定時，多由三境而出於定。一、由有境，二、由境境，三、由滅境。由此三境，於出定時，如其次第觸三種觸。緣於有境而出定時，無有我慢擾動其心。謂此為我、而起我慢，或計未來我當有等，乃至廣說。是故說言觸不動觸。緣於境境而出定時，無貪所有、無瞋所有、無癡所有。是故言觸無所有觸。緣於滅境而出定時，於一切相不思惟故，緣無相界。是故說言觸無相觸。
items.en: How, on emerging from the cessation attainment, does one touch three contacts — the unmoving contact, the nothingness contact, and the signless contact? On emerging, one mostly emerges by way of three objects: the object that is, the outer sense-objects, and the object of cessation. By these three, on emerging, one touches the three contacts in order. Emerging by way of the object that is, no self-conceit disturbs the mind — reckoning "this is I" and giving rise to self-conceit, or reckoning "I shall exist in the future," and so on — therefore it is called touching the unmoving contact. Emerging by way of the outer sense-objects, there is no greed's having, no hatred's having, no delusion's having — therefore it is called touching the nothingness contact. Emerging by way of the object of cessation, not attending to any sign, one takes the signless realm as object — therefore it is called touching the signless contact.

items.title: Closing the Survey: The Dhyānas, Liberations, Unifications, and Attainments

items.zh: 如是已說靜慮、解脫、等持、等至。
items.en: Thus have been explained the dhyānas, the liberations, the unifications, and the attainments.

blocks.text: The last reading of fascicle 12 describes the two "mindless" attainments: the attainment without perception, practised by non-Buddhists, and the **attainment of cessation**, which only noble ones enter. The second raises a famous puzzle: if all mind ceases, what keeps the body alive, and how does mind return? Yogācāra's answer is the ālayavijñāna.

"For one who has left the desire of the Universally-Pure heaven (the third dhyāna) but not higher desire, taking as its precondition the attention of permanently escaping perception": this is the **attainment without perception** (無想定). Its practitioners mistake the cessation of perception for liberation (Day 23). Master Cháng Bǎi: reborn in the corresponding heaven, one stays five hundred great eons; "in the final half-eon, the moment perception arises, one dies" and falls.

The **attainment of cessation** (滅盡定, *nirodha-samāpatti*) is entered only by noble ones. Venerable Miào Jìng: "This practitioner must be a Buddhist, and a non-returner; stream-enterers and once-returners can't enter it." It is preceded by the attention of "abiding at rest", not of escaping.

The formations cease in order. Master Cháng Bǎi: "verbal formation (applied and sustained thought) ceases in the second dhyāna; bodily formation (the breath) in the fourth; and mental formation (feeling and perception) in cessation." Entering through the peak of existence, one lets go even of that subtle mind.

In cessation all active minds cease. Why is consciousness said not to have left the body? "Because within the unspoiled material faculties there is the storehouse consciousness, which holds the seeds of the active consciousnesses and does not cease." This is one of the treatise's clearest arguments for the ālayavijñāna (Day 74): something must hold the body and the seeds when all six consciousnesses stop, or the meditator would simply be dead.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a desire-realm being cannot remain in cessation beyond seven days, because only the ālayavijñāna remains, without the nourishment of solid food, contact, or intention (Day 32's four foods).

The second puzzle: with no thought on entering and none on emerging, how does one come out? "Because one has beforehand well cultivated the mind." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Say at 11 p.m. he enters cessation, resolving: when the temple board is struck tomorrow morning, I'll come out." The resolve made beforehand acts as a seed.

On emerging, one touches three contacts: the unmoving, the signless, and the nothing-at-all. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Cheng Weishi Lun*, matches them to the three gateways of Day 89: entering through emptiness, one emerges with the unmoving contact; through wishlessness, the nothing-at-all; through signlessness, the signless.

"The dhyānas, liberations, unifications, and attainments have been explained." Fascicle 13 completes the Stage of Meditative Absorption with a gathering of essential sūtra passages, and then turns to the seventh stage, the stage that is *not* meditative absorption.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the no-perception attainment?
options: for one free of the third dhyāna's desire but not higher desire, preceded by the attention of permanently escaping perception, minds and mental factors cease
quiz.why: "For one who has left the desire of the Universally-Pure but not the higher desire, taking as its precondition the attention of permanent escape from perception, the minds and mental factors cease." Master Cháng Bǎi: "This no-perception attainment is practised by non-Buddhists; noble ones don't cultivate it."

quiz.q: Born in the no-perception heaven, "one only enters and does not emerge; when perception arises, one falls." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say of its lifespan?
options: five hundred great eons, about 499 without perception; in the last half-eon, once perception arises, one dies
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Five hundred great eons — about 499 without perception; in the final half-eon, the moment perception arises, one dies." He cites the *Vibhāṣā*'s monk who chose this "dung-heap concentration" over the Dharma's treasure.

quiz.q: Who enters the cessation attainment, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: only Buddhists, and only non-returners and above; stream-enterers and once-returners cannot
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "This practitioner must be a Buddhist, and a non-returner; stream-enterers and once-returners can't enter cessation"; even the seventh consciousness's self-grasping is stilled. The text: for one free of the desire of nothingness, minds and factors cease.

quiz.q: On entering cessation, the three formations cease in order. What sequence does Master Cháng Bǎi summarise?
options: verbal formation ceases at the second dhyāna, bodily at the fourth, and mental (feeling and perception) at cessation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "In sum: speech-formation ceases in the second dhyāna, body-formation in the fourth, and the mental formations of feeling and perception in cessation." Venerable Miào Jìng: speech is coarsest, body next, mind subtlest. On emerging they arise in reverse.

quiz.q: In cessation all minds cease — why is consciousness said not to leave the body?
options: within the unspoiled faculties, the storehouse consciousness holding the seeds of active consciousness doesn't cease, and they later arise from it
quiz.why: "Because within the unspoiled material faculties there is the storehouse-consciousness, which holds the seeds of the active consciousnesses and is not extinguished; so that afterwards those dharmas arise again from it." Master Cháng Bǎi: the question arises from the six-consciousness view of the śrāvakas.

quiz.q: How long can a desire-realm being stay in cessation, per Master Cháng Bǎi, and why?
options: no more than seven days — only the ālaya remains, without material food, contact, or intention as nourishment
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "A desire-realm being can't stay in cessation beyond seven days, because only the ālaya remains — no material food, contact, or intention." Venerable Miào Jìng tells of a monk who died on emerging after more than seven days.

quiz.q: On emerging from cessation one touches three contacts. How does Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the Cheng weishi lun, correlate them?
options: to the three concentrations — entering via emptiness, one emerges touching the unmoving contact; via wishlessness, the nothingness contact
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Entering cessation through emptiness, one emerges touching the unmoving contact; entering through wishlessness, the nothingness contact" — and through signlessness, the signless contact. The text: no self-conceit, no greed-hatred-delusion, and the signless realm, respectively.
